# Pi-Bifrost

> Model-routing extension for the Pi coding agent. You configure tier pools and strategies. Bifrost selects a model from that policy, then Pi runs the real provider/model.

## Links

- Landing page: https://iamaamir.github.io/pi-bifrost/

- Guide: https://github.com/iamaamir/pi-bifrost/blob/main/docs/guide/index.md
- Installation: https://github.com/iamaamir/pi-bifrost/blob/main/docs/guide/getting-started.md
- Routing controls: https://github.com/iamaamir/pi-bifrost/blob/main/docs/guide/routing-controls.md

- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/pi-bifrost

## Install

Requires Pi 1.0.1 or newer and at least one authenticated provider model available in Pi.

```sh
pi install npm:pi-bifrost
```

Inside Pi, run `/bifrost init`. Init reuses recent probe results or sends small requests to available models, which can incur usage or rate limits. It proposes a configuration and writes it after confirmation. Then run `/bifrost classifier` to select a classifier backend, or `/bifrost classifier off` to use rules and the default tier without a classifier call.

## Route

```text
prompt → tier → configured model pool → reliability filter → strategy → Pi model
```

A tier is selected from a tier prefix, rule, local classification cache, optional classifier, or configured default. An exact-model rule can bypass the tier. Strategies include `first`, `fastest` (current list order, which init can sort by probe speed), `cheapest`, `cheapest_input`, `cheapest_output`, `largest_context`, and `random`. Persistent circuits skip repeatedly failing models on future turns and later allow controlled recovery. In Auto, an explicit usage-limit rejection can receive one retry on another configured eligible model only when Pi proves all failed attempts were empty, from the same model, and exactly omitted, with no tool activity. Pi's own bounded retry may run first. Set `reliability.retryOnAllowanceExhausted: false` to disable Bifrost failover. See `docs/adr/0023-bounded-allowance-recovery.md`.

Physical selection is the default: Bifrost activates Pi's provider/model before generation. Selecting `bifrost/auto` in Pi's `/model` picker opts into per-request physical dispatch using the same routing policy. Pi's footer shows `bifrost/auto → provider/model`; assistant messages record the physical model that answered. Tool continuations and retries remain on the model that started the turn. Selecting a physical model pins it for the session.

## Controls

- `/bifrost preview <prompt>` resolves a route without generating or activating a model. An enabled classifier may receive the preview prompt. A leading tier name in the preview prompt is not applied as an override. Use `/bifrost preview --json <prompt>` for one machine-readable result line prefixed with `[bifrost-json] ` on stderr.
- A message starting with a configured single-word lowercase alphabetic tier name uses that tier for one turn. The prefix is removed before the model sees the message. Pinned sessions ignore tier prefixes.
- `/bifrost pin` keeps the current physical model for the session. `/bifrost unpin` resumes routing.
- `/bifrost off` and `/bifrost on` disable or enable routing. Off or pin exits Auto using the last dispatched physical model, or a default-tier model before any dispatch.
- `/bifrost classifier test` makes a fresh classifier request; `/bifrost classifier status` shows safe operational state.

## Optional tier classifiers

Classifiers choose a tier, never the exact provider model. Backends: `prompt` (a Pi chat model), `typesafe` (direct TypeSafe/Jev transport), and `pi-native` (Pi's `classify()` API and catalog, shown only when supported). Explicit `classifier.backend` wins. If absent, Bifrost detects Pi-managed TypeSafe credentials, then `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`, and otherwise chooses prompt. The first routed request reports the detected backend and reason. Disable classification for rules/default-only routing. An enabled classifier receives the current prompt and tier criteria, not conversation history or provider model pools by default; preview can also invoke it. Confidence is not a correctness guarantee.

## Limits

Bifrost is not a model proxy or multi-agent orchestrator. Its local classification cache stores normalized prompt terms, not answers. Treat those terms as potentially sensitive. Reliability circuits are not authoritative quota enforcement. Switching models can fragment provider prompt-cache locality. Pin one model when context continuity matters. Bifrost does not guarantee better code, lower cost, lower latency, or cache savings.
